CAT.rationale: CAT is a genuinely strong franchise with dominant market position, a secular AI data center power tailwind, and a record $62.7B backlog providing multi-year revenue visibility. Q1 2026 showed +22.2% YoY revenue growth and +30.2% EPS growth. However, the stock is priced at an extreme 47.6× trailing PE (up from 18.8× one year ago — a 2.5× multiple expansion) with a 2.1% earnings yield that is less than half the 4.49% 10-year Treasury yield. The vast majority of the stock's ~150% gain over 12 months has been multiple expansion, not earnings delivery. Trailing net margin has already compressed from 15.7% to 13.3%, Resource Industries profit plunged 39% YoY, tariff headwinds of $2.2–2.6B are projected for 2026, and the yield curve is flattening (10Y-2Y spread at 0.35%) — a classic late-cycle signal for cyclicals. Michael Burry has disclosed a short position citing unsustainable valuation. A reversion to even 25× PE on current EPS implies ~47% downside. The balance sheet's 4.1× liability-to-equity ratio amplifies risk in a stress scenario. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating margin trajectory, extreme valuation vs own history, and multiple near-term downside catalysts (tariff costs, curve flattening, Burry disclosure, consensus targets well below current price).
